slots.questionIntent: A regional utility receives 18,000 free-form outage emails each day. Operations wants to cut triage time to 15 minutes per incident, while equipment switching remains outside the model's authority. Which initial solution best translates the business problem into a production scope?
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: Triage speed is the measured outcome.
Equipment switching remains outside Claude's authority.

expectedOutcome.resolution: The scope starts with the measurable triage job and makes the authority boundary executable. It gives the team an observable first release instead of treating more autonomy or more training as the business requirement.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: State the business result, authority limit, and acceptance evidence before selecting a model pattern or implementation investment.
slots.decisiveBoundary: The bounded design leaves switching with existing controls, which limits immediate automation but reduces operational risk while the team learns where autonomy is justified.
slots.transferBoundary: Use the same framing for claims or support: name the work unit to improve, the authority the system has, and the evidence that will show improvement.

testedProperties: Anthropic recommends starting with the simplest solution and adding agentic complexity only when it is needed, because agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance.

overlapExclusions: Other objectives do not own the business-problem-framing decision.
The bounded design leaves switching with existing controls, which limits immediate automation but reduces operational risk while the team learns where autonomy is justified.
slots.maintenanceRisk: Recheck source mechanisms and the official objective when documentation or guide changes.
slots.simulationOwnershipRationale: The decisive skill is business-problem-framing, mapped to domain 1, objective bullet 1.

slots.questionIntent: A hospital scheduling team asks for a Claude assistant to “improve productivity.” The prototype has a polished chat screen, reviewers disagree about usefulness, and there is no current-process baseline. What should the architect do next?
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: The request names an aspiration but no testable outcome.
The prototype can change before production investment.

expectedOutcome.resolution: The team cannot diagnose a productivity effect until it defines the work unit and compares it with current practice. A task-specific evaluation should precede prompt or architecture changes.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: Do not treat interface polish, tool count, or subjective enthusiasm as the business requirement; define the behavior change and evidence first.
slots.decisiveBoundary: Discovery and evaluation delay broad rollout, but they prevent optimization of a system whose value cannot yet be demonstrated.
slots.transferBoundary: Whenever a sponsor says productivity or transformation, ask what behavior changes, for whom, and how the current process will be compared.

testedProperties: Anthropic's guide says to establish clear success criteria and empirical tests before improving a prompt.

overlapExclusions: Other objectives do not own the business-problem-framing decision.
Discovery and evaluation delay broad rollout, but they prevent optimization of a system whose value cannot yet be demonstrated.
slots.maintenanceRisk: Recheck source mechanisms and the official objective when documentation or guide changes.
slots.simulationOwnershipRationale: The decisive skill is business-problem-framing, mapped to domain 1, objective bullet 1.

slots.questionIntent: A benefits assistant must explain eligibility while deterministic, versioned income and date rules remain authoritative. Which design puts Claude at the right boundary?
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: Eligibility thresholds and effective dates are authoritative outside the model.
The assistant should explain a result and expose uncertainty rather than invent a determination.

expectedOutcome.resolution: The deterministic service owns the consequence-bearing calculation; Claude performs the language work that benefits from context and can hand off an exception.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: Keep the policy decision outside the model and validate the explanatory output; this reduces model flexibility but protects reproducibility and appeals.
slots.decisiveBoundary: This division gives up automatic eligibility decisions, but it keeps the appealable calculation reproducible while preserving useful explanation.
slots.transferBoundary: The same boundary applies when a model summarizes a regulated calculation: computation and authorization remain in the system of record.

testedProperties: Anthropic describes the augmented LLM as an LLM enhanced with capabilities such as retrieval, tools, and memory, with interfaces tailored to the use case.

overlapExclusions: Other objectives do not own the business-problem-framing decision.
This division gives up automatic eligibility decisions, but it keeps the appealable calculation reproducible while preserving useful explanation.
slots.maintenanceRisk: Recheck source mechanisms and the official objective when documentation or guide changes.
slots.simulationOwnershipRationale: The decisive skill is business-problem-framing, mapped to domain 1, objective bullet 1.

slots.questionIntent: A retailer is redesigning returns operations. Store staff read customer messages, check policy, and prepare a recommendation; a time study shows policy lookup consumes most handling time, and a supervisor retains refund authorization. Which TWO decisions best translate this problem into a coherent first release? Select TWO.
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: The release should target policy lookup time and recommendation quality.
Refund authorization remains with a supervisor.

expectedOutcome.resolution: The first release pairs the measured bottleneck with an observable workflow and preserves the supervisor's consequential decision. Both value evidence and responsibility are explicit.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: Translate automation into a target work step and an authority statement before broadening data or permissions.
slots.decisiveBoundary: A narrower release defers refund automation but lowers exposure and produces evidence for the next investment.
slots.transferBoundary: For any operational assistant, pair a value measure with what the model may prepare and what a person or deterministic service must decide.

testedProperties: Anthropic recommends clear success criteria and empirical tests before prompt improvement, making the business objective testable.

overlapExclusions: Other objectives do not own the business-problem-framing decision.
A narrower release defers refund automation but lowers exposure and produces evidence for the next investment.
slots.maintenanceRisk: Recheck source mechanisms and the official objective when documentation or guide changes.
slots.simulationOwnershipRationale: The decisive skill is business-problem-framing, mapped to domain 1, objective bullet 1.

slots.questionIntent: A utility billing service receives 200,000 normalized records per day. A deterministic rules service already validates them in 40 ms p95, and all required fields are structured. The team proposes adding Claude to classify each record before posting. Which decision is best?
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: All required inputs are structured and the validated rules service meets the 40 ms p95 target.
No measured language task is missing from the current posting path.

expectedOutcome.resolution: Introducing a model adds latency and an unmeasured failure mode without a language-shaped problem to solve. The existing deterministic path should remain canonical while evidence guides any later language capability.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: Match the solution mechanism to the information shape and outcome; model presence is not itself a business benefit.
slots.decisiveBoundary: The design gives up speculative model coverage but protects a proven latency and correctness path and avoids redundant spend.
slots.transferBoundary: Before adding an LLM, ask whether every input and decision rule are already deterministic and whether any language task has measurable value.

testedProperties: Anthropic recommends the simplest solution that meets the need and notes that added agentic complexity trades latency and cost for performance; the no-LLM conclusion follows from this scenario’s fully deterministic task.

overlapExclusions: Other objectives do not own the business-problem-framing decision.
The design gives up speculative model coverage but protects a proven latency and correctness path and avoids redundant spend.
slots.maintenanceRisk: Recheck source mechanisms and the official objective when documentation or guide changes.
slots.simulationOwnershipRationale: The decisive skill is business-problem-framing, mapped to domain 1, objective bullet 1.

slots.questionIntent: A warehouse alert service must emit a structured alert within 100 ms p95 from event codes. Incident commanders also gain material value from a Claude narrative over unstructured incident notes, but measured Claude completion is about 600 ms. The notes are stored as an immutable, versioned snapshot. Which design meets both needs?
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: The alert deadline is 100 ms p95 and the immediate alert uses structured event codes.
Claude narrative latency is measured at about 600 ms; the source snapshot has a version and freshness boundary.

expectedOutcome.resolution: The value-bearing narrative is real but its measured latency cannot satisfy the immediate alert contract. Separate the deterministic deadline path from an asynchronous, freshness-labeled language result.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: The split path adds coordination and a stale-result state, but it preserves both the operational deadline and the measured business value of narrative analysis.
slots.decisiveBoundary: Use synchronous Claude only if a paired benchmark shows completion and freshness fit the 100 ms contract; otherwise retain the asynchronous boundary.
slots.transferBoundary: When a language result is valuable but misses a hard deadline, isolate it behind a versioned asynchronous contract instead of weakening the deadline.

testedProperties: Anthropic recommends starting with the simplest solution and adding agentic complexity only when it is needed, because agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance.

overlapExclusions: Other objectives do not own the business-problem-framing decision.
Use synchronous Claude only if a paired benchmark shows completion and freshness fit the 100 ms contract; otherwise retain the asynchronous boundary.
slots.maintenanceRisk: Recheck source mechanisms and the official objective when documentation or guide changes.
slots.simulationOwnershipRationale: The decisive skill is business-problem-framing, mapped to domain 1, objective bullet 1.

slots.questionIntent:
A billing service receives free-form technician notes alongside normalized codes. The deterministic posting rules meet their latency target for coded records, but the notes contain the only description of an unclassified fault.

Which architecture addresses the note bottleneck while preserving the posting authority?
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: Free text is the only ambiguous input; normalized codes already meet the latency target.
The existing rules service must remain the authority for validation and posting.

slots.questionIntent: Metadata and redacted timing are insufficient to reproduce a high-memory incident. The organization has explicitly authorized a private diagnostic sample with a named operator, restricted storage, and deletion date; support does not need routine prompt retention. Select TWO actions.
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: Lower-sensitivity metadata and redacted reproduction were tried first.
Authorization, access, restricted storage, and deletion controls are recorded.
Routine telemetry does not need prompt retention.

expectedOutcome.resolution: Detailed diagnostics are justified only as a bounded, explicitly authorized exception after redacted evidence is insufficient; storage, access, purpose, deletion, and redacted defaults keep the exposure controlled.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: Normal full capture creates unnecessary exposure, while blanket refusal ignores a proportionate authorized investigation; indefinite retention exceeds the approved purpose and deletion boundary.
slots.decisiveBoundary: Without named authorization, restricted storage, or a deletion rule, remain with redacted metadata and safe-mode reproduction rather than collecting detailed diagnostics.
slots.transferBoundary: Escalate sensitive diagnostics only through an authorized, purpose-limited capture with controlled access and deletion, while routine telemetry remains redacted.

slots.questionIntent: The provider returns a response that passes the requested structured-output schema, but the CI consumer rejects it because the consumer still expects an older field version. Request latency and provider availability are normal. What should be repaired first?
materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: The provider response and transport status are valid.
The consumer schema version and parser error are available.
The failure occurs at the downstream contract boundary.

expectedOutcome.resolution: A valid provider response does not satisfy an older downstream schema; the producer-consumer contract must be compared and versioned before provider availability is investigated.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: Provider retries, model changes, and timeouts cannot repair a consumer that rejects a valid response; accepting both schemas without versioning moves the failure downstream.
slots.decisiveBoundary: If the provider response were invalid or an HTTP error reached CI before parsing, provider error classification and request correlation would be the relevant diagnostic branch.
slots.transferBoundary: When transport and provider output are valid but a consumer rejects the schema, repair and test the versioned interface at the producer-consumer boundary.

materialEvidenceOrConstraintChanged: The native-versus-JavaScript memory classification is available.
The JavaScript heap is within its normal range.
Lower-sensitivity runtime and repository evidence can be collected first.

expectedOutcome.resolution: The measured memory class makes an ordinary JavaScript heap snapshot low-yield; native-memory evidence directs the next investigation to runtime or repository loading while sensitive capture remains conditional.

slots.errorModelOrFailureMode: A detailed JavaScript artifact does not explain native allocations, while model changes or routine heap capture change or broaden the investigation without addressing the measured resource class.
slots.decisiveBoundary: If JavaScript heap usage dominated and remained high after safe-mode and clean-session checks, a private heap snapshot could be appropriate under the documented sensitive-data handling.
slots.transferBoundary: Choose diagnostics by measured resource class; reserve sensitive, detailed artifacts for the class they can actually explain.
